title: Launch decision lattice + KPI tracker
content:
Purpose:
A compact, actionable decision lattice and KPI tracker to guide staged feature launches (alpha -> beta -> GA). Designed to combine hard metric gates with operational readiness checks so product, infra, and SRE teams can make deterministic go/no-go decisions and document rollbacks and mitigations.

How to use this sheet (quick):
- Populate the tracker rows for each feature or route you plan to ship.
- Fill metric targets, measurement queries, owners, and contingency actions.
- During canary/beta, update 'Current value' daily; update RAG manually and capture short notes under 'Blocker / action'.
- Use the Decision Rules block below to translate metric trend into required actions.

Tracker columns (one row per launch item):
- Feature: short name
- Jira: ticket key
- Phase: alpha | beta | ga
- Owner: primary responsible (name + pager)
- Status: on_track | at_risk | blocked | rolled_back | live
- KPI target (accept): short phrase + threshold (e.g. API success >= 99.5%)
- KPI threshold (warn/critical): e.g. warn: 0.5% errors, critical: 2% errors
- Measurement query: reference to analytics query/console metric (logQL / SQL / Redwood Console route id)
- Current value: last measured (date-stamped)
- RAG: green / amber / red
- Blocker / action: short note (who to ping, immediate mitigations)
- Next action: e.g., pause rollout, increase capacity, apply feature-flag rollback
- Due date: planned decision date for the next cadence check

Canonical KPIs and suggested acceptance thresholds (customize per product):
- API Success Rate (5m rolling): accept >= 99.5%; warn < 99.0%; critical < 98.0%
- Latency p50/p95 (in ms for the route): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 450ms for GA; for beta p95 <= 700ms
- Error budget burn (per day): accept <= 0.2% of budget; critical > 0.8%
- Cost per 1k generated tokens: target <= $0.30 for common routes; if > $0.60 evaluate quantization/trim prompts
- Model quality regression (eval set): delta BLEU/ROUGE or custom eval score within -2% of baseline; if worse, gate
- Traffic-scalability signals: steady CPU/GPU utilization < 75% at steady-state; if > 85% consider capacity bump
- User-facing fallbacks: fallback success rate >= 95% (if fallback exists)

Decision Rules (deterministic lattice):
- Green: All critical KPIs within accept. Continue rollout to next phase on scheduled cadence.
- Amber: Any warn-level hit sustained > 30m and trending worse. Hold rollout, open incident channel, remediate. Re-evaluate after mitigation window (1–4 hours).
- Red (critical): Any critical KPI violation sustained > 5m OR sudden spike in incidents. Immediately pause rollout, enable automatic fallback (if configured), and start rollback runbook. Notify SRE/infra/product on-call and exec on-call if GA.

Canary-specific rules:
- Canary sample: min 1% traffic or 1000 requests/min for 2 consecutive 10-minute windows to validate distribution-sensitive bugs.
- Priority checks during canary: API success, p95 latency, tail error patterns (5xx vs 4xx), memory OOMs, KV cache hit rate, model token generation delta (unexpected hallucination rate).
- If any backend OOM or GPU preemption occurs twice in 1 hour, auto-roll back to previous model/revision.

Rollout cadence & meeting runbook:
- Pre-launch (T-7 days): confirm observability dashboards, logging retention, alert routing, billing alerts, security sign-off.
- Dry-run (T-3 days): run synthetic traffic at 1x expected baseline for 60 minutes; validate traces and error classification.
- Day-of (T-0): launch owner posts hourly status updates in #prod-launch Slack channel for first 8 hours; SRE posts latency/cost summaries at 2h, 4h, 8h; product posts adoption metrics at 4h, 24h.
- Post-launch (T+1 to T+7): daily retrospective notes captured; KPI trends tracked; consider A/B adjustments or rollout acceleration if safe.

Preflight checklist (pre-requirements for moving from beta -> GA):
- [ ] SLA definition reviewed and accepted by legal + sales
- [ ] Observability: dashboards live, alerts smoke-tested, trace sampling set
- [ ] Cost guardrails: daily cost-alerts on unexpected token spike configured
- [ ] Security: threat model review done, data flow diagram on Confluence, KMS/HSM keys validated for private deploys
- [ ] Compliance: PII check complete, audit logging enabled where required
- [ ] Rollback plan: feature-flag path validated, infra-level revert validated in staging
- [ ] Support ops: runbook published, escalation matrix sent to support and on-call

Contingency actions (examples mapped to metric triggers):
- Latency p95 breach: reduce concurrency on the route, switch to smaller batch size, deploy a quantized variant, or temporarily reduce TTL caching to reduce tail pressure.
- Error spike (5xx): divert traffic to previous stable model variant, enable immediate fallback responses, open incident with triage template.
- Cost spike: activate throttling at gateway, reduce max_tokens setting, or adjust sampling strategy.

Postmortem / regression triggers:
- If a launch results in > 1% user-visible defects or > 10% cost overrun vs projection for 24h, schedule postmortem within 48 hours.
- Capture: timeline, metric graphs, root cause hypotheses, mitigations, follow-ups with owners and due dates.

Minimal queries & dashboards to wire before canary:
- Route success rate (5m, 1h), errors by status code, errors by model-version, latency p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, memory OOM events, cost per token by route.
- Eval suite automation: nightly regression checks against core prompt-set (capture mean/median score and outliers).

Example tracker row (text example to paste into the sheet):
Feature: "streaming-summaries" | Jira: PROD-1123 | Phase: beta | Owner: Priya Patel (pager: Priya) | Status: on_track | KPI target: API success >= 99.5% / p95 <= 600ms | Measurement: Redwood Console route streaming-summaries v2 | Current value: success=99.7% p95=520ms (2026-03-01) | RAG: green | Blocker/action: none | Next action: scale to 5% traffic on 2026-03-03 | Due date: 2026-03-03

Notes and common gotchas:
- Baselines matter: compare to time-of-day and traffic mix; sudden degradation during peak hours can be masked if you look at global averages.
- Quality gates must be tied to small, curated eval sets (example prompts) and also blind production checks — both are necessary.
- Don’t shortcut rollback validation: feature flags are cheap insurance. Validate the flag path at least once pre-launch.

Ownership & contacts (recommended default on-call list):
- Launch owner: Priya Patel (product-ops)
- SRE lead: Evan Liu
- ML infra: Jonah Kim
- Applied ML quality: Mariana Soto
- Support ops: Sana Ahmed

Appendix: quick copy/paste checks for the launch channel message (hourly):
- [Hour X update] Phase: beta (X%) | Success: 99.7% | p95: 520ms | Errors: 0.12% | Cost: $0.28 / 1k tokens | Actions: none | Notes: increasing to 5% at next window

End of sheet. Keep this doc as the single source-of-truth for the feature's launch decisions and link the row to the canonical Jira and Confluence pages. If anything is ambiguous, escalate to SRE lead and product-ops for deterministic arbitration.
